posts.cooked:
Ashdia is presumably a recent development, but when they talked about a prince of despair, my immediate thought was that Gloomweaver’s discordian magic power over Despair was stolen from some primordial ancient Aeternal prince thereof, whose domain then lay fallow for aeons, up until the very goth/emo Ashdia gathered those ancient remnants of power unto herself. Because this would be the demon prince version of finding a gnarly feathered mask in an antique shop.

Ps, Wrath is understood by a lot of Bible scholars to include despair, which is thought of as anger against God for failing to provide hope, and so I like the idea that Ashdia is like Abbados’s cousin or something.

By the way, I’m gonna cape for Acedia a bit, because I see sloth as flat refusal to move, a determination to stay put and waste no energy, and listlessness as movement in various aimless directions with no plan, never getting anywhere and squandering one’s energy in the process. Frankly, if Gluttony and Greed and Envy can all be separate sins, then certainly these two are good enough. I was disappointed that Christoher’s dissertation didn’t make any mention of the fact that Lust is a translation error and the original sin was Luxury (again, somehow distinct from Greed and Sloth).

This is one of my favorite topics, and pretty definitely the best episode since the hiatus for me. I will be listening again soon to relocate at least two further topics I plan to expound upon.

“The Autoverse is Transformers”. Dude, there’s literally a movie called Cars. No alien robots necessary.

Vainglory isn’t pride, it’s specifically prideful boasting, or just boasting in general. It doesn’t mean YOU think highly of yourself, it means you want others to think you’re great, so you’re lying through your teeth. It relates to Pride very similarly to how Envy relates to Greed.

Argh, lost my pause point. Neither of these was among the two big points I want to speak on, so I’ll be back on yet another day, after listening to this episode’s first half for a third time. It has been among my favorites, but I wonder how long it can stay that way.
